diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, if $G$ has a unique fixed-point, then $(\widehat{\mu}_t)_{t\in\N_0}$ converges $\PROB$-almost surely in $\CW_2$ to the Wasserstein barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ with weights $w_1,\ldots,w_K$.

We would like to remark that the operator~$G$ in (ef{eqn: G-operator}) does not always have a unique fixed-point for general input probability measures $
u_1,\ldots,
u_K\in\CP_{2,\mathrm{ac}}(\R^d)$; see, e.g., Example~3.1 of \citep{alvarez2016fixed} for a concrete counterexample. It is known that $G$ has a unique fixed-point when $
u_1,\ldots,
u_K$ belong to the same parametric family of elliptical distributions \citep[Section~4]{alvarez2016fixed}, e.g., Gaussian distributions. However, to the best of our knowledge, sufficient conditions to guarantee the uniqueness of the fixed-point of~$G$ for non-parametric $
u_1,\ldots,
u_K$ is still an open problem.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contributions claim the algorithm is provably convergent to the W2 barycenter. The formal theorem only establishes precompactness and that accumulation points are fixed points of G; convergence to the barycenter is conditional on G having a unique fixed point. The paper itself notes that uniqueness for non-parametric measures is open, so the unconditional claim is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the abstract and contribution statements to say convergence to the barycenter holds when G has a unique fixed point (or add sufficient conditions for uniqueness).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee of almost sure convergence to the barycenter for general continuous non-parametric measures is not established; only the conditional version is proved.
issues.title: Abstract overstates unconditional convergence to the barycenter
issues.why_classification: The formal theorem remains valid, but the main advertised convergence guarantee is materially overstated; the repair is a scope qualification rather than new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem unique barycenter only yields $\bar{\mu}\in\CP_{2,\mathrm{ac}}$ when at least one input measure has bounded density. Theorem G-property assumes only $\nu_k\in\CP_{2,\mathrm{ac}}$, so the conclusion that $\bar{\mu}\in\CP_{2,\mathrm{ac}}$ (needed for $G(\bar{\mu})$ to be defined) is not justified by the cited result.

failure_location.quote: The unique $\CW_2$-barycenter $\bar{\mu} \in \CP_{2, \mathrm{ac}}(\R^d)$ (see Theorem~\ref{thm: unique barycenter}) of $\nu_1, \dots, \nu_K$ with weights $w_1,\ldots,w_K$ is a fixed-point of $G$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that at least one $\nu_k$ has bounded density (or assume $\bar{\mu}\in\CP_{2,\mathrm{ac}}$) to Theorem G-property.
issues.overall_effect: The preliminary fixed-point theorem is overbroad. Its later uses occur under the stronger $\CM^q$ assumptions, where bounded densities are present, so the main algorithm's convergence results are not invalidated.
issues.title: Theorem G-property omits bounded-density hypothesis for absolute continuity of barycenter
issues.why_classification: The missing hypothesis is already satisfied in the main setting $\CM^q$, so the main results survive; the repair is a local hypothesis addition to a preliminary theorem.
